correctness.rationale: On any connected allocation, K=N(tr(L+J/N)^-1-1) is strictly convex in all independent edge weights. Dihedral symmetry yields equal weights within the two price orbits. Exact wheel spectrum gives K=m(1+ct)F_m(t)/B; the derivative at zero is m^2(c-2-2/m), while constrained strict convexity proves a unique global allocation. The Poisson-kernel sum and Taylor expansion establish the fixed-c and c=2+kappa/m limits, including the boundary c=c*. The shipped standard-library checker passed 260 exact-rational and supporting Fourier consistency checks; 24 unconstrained numerical optimizations also reproduced the objective bounds, but neither finite test is taken as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem asks when a purchasable cycle of redundant shortcut links is economically dispensable despite a common hub. The parameter c is the natural relative unit procurement price, not an arbitrary statistic. The sharp cutoff 2+2/m provides an exact purchase decision for every wheel, while the nontrivial m^-1 price window and quadratic m^-2 savings quantify the large-network sensitivity hidden by the already-known equal-price solution. The complete theorem includes all independent edge allocations, not just a guessed symmetric design.
